raw_response:
I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. I am 73, so I will not chase crops that need too much hand labor or market judgment. I know wheat and maize best, the machines are easy to hire, the sales are steady, and in Quzhou County this rotation fits the water, the soil, and the season. In autumn I will sow winter wheat on all my land, use improved seed, put most of the phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, split the nitrogen so the crop stands well, and irrigate mainly at the key stages instead of watering too many times. After wheat harvest in early summer, I will plant summer maize right away, use hybrid seed for stable yield, keep the field management simple, and control weeds, insects, and disease only as needed. I will do moderate fertilization, not excessive fertilization, because I want steady output and lower risk, not fancy management.
